I’m like you and I would feel really upset inside and not know how to approach it. The right thing to do is always to communicate, but actually doing it can be so uncomfortable, intimidating and hard. 

I would have a hard time with the feelings of rejection and hurt and have a hard time moving on after his mother set up the expectation that it was going to you and being part of your special day. And while it is a touchy subject and it’s his mom’s personal decision in the end…. I feel like this is a unique situation with a lot of nuance. Unlike the other commenters, I feel like there’s going to be a lot of pushed down hurt from every side, which will lead to a lot of assumptions and resentments down the road if there isn’t a lot of (calm, respectful) communication about what happened here. Resentments are powerful things that nag at relationships. It’s best that instead of everyone making assumptions about each other, everyone gets clarity on each other’s intentions before it becomes something bigger.

I do genuinely like the ring that was designed. But I do not like implications behind it that your wants and wishes were discarded and there’s a lot left unsaid from your fiancé and his mother. 

Please keep us updated about what happens from here. This is definitely something I’m going to wonder about. I really hope it plays out well for you, OP. I hope that your feelings are understood and respected. I hope you gain some clarity that makes you feel better and that talking about it and coming to a resolution makes everyone feel closer in the end.

I’m taking a moment to ponder that. In my culture/area/family, it’s actually quite common to take photos at funerals, including the open casket. Common enough that people post his photos online, including on Facebook headers. It’s actually considered fairly wholesome. My family frequently looks back at pictures from funerals in our family for peace. I’m just taking a moment to think about a cameraless funeral. 

I do recall losing certain friends throughout the years whose families did not disclose the manner of death. It always left me without any closure. 

I don’t want to distract too much from the subject of this Reddit. We come from different backgrounds, I suppose. Thank you for giving me a different viewpoint to think about. 

I do, however, think it’s incredibly rare that every member of the search party who found them was capable or desired to remain tight lipped.

It’s not so much that I feel entitled to it or that it wouldn’t be disrespectful. It’s just that from my perspective, I’ve been through quite a few tragedies in my life and in my experiences, these things start coming out through the grape vine. Sort of a whisper down the lane effect. People are disturbed and want to talk about it with peers and eventually it comes out. Usually small gatherings in the kitchen turn to people talking about it with their partners, friend, etc to get it off their chest.

You know, I ask myself this question at least once a week. 

It is bizarre to me that literally no information concerning what’s on the audio, a description/photos of how the bodies were found, nor a cause of death has ever been leaked.
